question: Can a fixed native group reduce unnecessary output while preserving complete-program correctness, and how does it compare with a simple instruction?
prerequisite: N39 must close with passing guards and its prescribed groups actually available. If its full-site or strict matching stage stops before selection, leave N40 unexecuted. A failed role primary stays failed; program utility is a separate question.
fixed_edit: Outgoing-column factor zero on exactly the selected native group and both prescribed random controls. No new coordinates, fitted strengths, incoming weights, bridge, transplant or training.
conditions: original with one fixed instruction omitting comments and docstrings
control_interpretation: Report the simple instruction alongside every edit. If it works as well or better, state that. Do not attribute token reductions on already-wrong programs to useful coding efficiency.
engineering: Require physical-column versus all-position activation-zero equivalence, exact restore and declared parameter-version changes before utility. No optimizer or gradient update.
limits: Conditional intent, not a model outcome. Existing strict retention is weak. All cases and gains/losses remain. Reused development requires fresh confirmation. Token counts do not establish hardware acceleration or wall-clock speedup. Raw task and control wording remain private.
